transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Sofia (Argon Head of AI), Liam (Argon Platform), Priya (Argon Security)
Meeting ID: ff-20260807-argon-001

Summary:
Quick POC scoping focused on integration planning: SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, and structured output extraction. Discussed success criteria (latency/throughput/accuracy), workload sizing and benchmark plan, security requirements, and a 4-week pilot timeline.

Topics:
- Integration paths: Redwood SDK vs OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints
- Function calling / tool invocation semantics and structured JSON outputs
- Benchmarking plan: datasets, metrics, infra (hosted vs dedicated)
- Security: VPC, SSO, SOC2, KMS
- Success criteria and timeline for 4-week pilot

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 45ish minutes, will do intros quick then jump into the poc scope.
[00:18] Sofia (Argon): hi, sofia here, excited, we've been looking at a few vendors, want to validate integration pattern for our product tagging and receipt ingestion flows.
[00:29] Liam (Argon): liam, platform eng, i'll be doing most of the integration work.
[00:35] Priya (Argon): priya, security — will focus on data residency + sso requirements.
[00:40] Ethan (Redwood): ethan from redwood infra team, i'll cover SDK examples and the benchmark plan. quick note: i'm going to reference both our native SDKs and our OpenAI-compatible endpoints which many teams find easiest to integrate.
[01:05] Maya (Redwood): high level goal — Argon wants to run a 4-week pilot to validate accuracy of structured extraction from receipts and invoices and understand cost/latency at 50 rps esper.. uh 50 reqs per second baseline, with spikes to 150. does that sound right?
[01:23] Sofia (Argon): yes that's right. success criteria we care about: field-level extraction accuracy > 95% on key fields (total, merchant, date), end-to-end P95 latency < 250ms for small docs, and predictable cost under X (we'll share numbers).
[01:40] Maya (Redwood): perfect, that gives us measurable targets. quick question on doc size distribution? small receipts vs 2-page invoices?
[01:52] Liam (Argon): roughly 70% receipts (short), 30% invoices average 1-2 pages. sample set we can provide ~50k rows including OCR outputs.
[02:05] Ethan (Redwood): good to know — for that distribution we recommended model variants with optimized attention and kv-cache handling; for high throughput we can do continuous batching and prefix caching. note: if you go dedicated we can guarantee throughput and lower tail latency.
[02:25] Priya (Argon): security wise we need SOC2 + customer's KMS for encryption, and SSO with SAML. can redwood support a VPC private deployment?
[02:40] Maya (Redwood): yes — Redwood Private supports customer VPC and on-prem options, and we integrate with KMS/HSM for key management. we'll include our compliance pack; it's in the security docset.
[02:55] Sofia (Argon): thanks. on integration, our product team prefers an OpenAI-compatible interface because we already have a small shim for that. is your OpenAI-compatible endpoint fully feature-par with your native SDK (eg streaming, function calling)?
[03:15] Ethan (Redwood): good question — our OpenAI-compatible endpoints support text generation, chat, embeddings and function/tool calling, but there are a few mapping differences for advanced batching and some real-time autoscaling knobs that are more straightforward via our SDK. function calling semantics are preserved — you can define tool schemas and we return structured JSON.
[03:36] Liam (Argon): can you show an example?
[03:40] Ethan (Redwood): sure i'll paste a quick snippet after the call, but essentially you can call POST /v1/chat/completions with function definitions; we return the function name and a JSON payload in the response; same as OpenAI. with our SDK you get helpers for streaming chunked JSON, automatic retry, and built-in request coalescing.
[04:05] Maya (Redwood): to be concrete — for the POC you can either hit our OpenAI-compatible endpoint and reuse your existing shim, or wire in our SDK (node/python) which will likely cut dev time for retries and structured parsing. both valid.
[04:20] Sofia (Argon): leaning to OpenAI-compatible to reduce changes in our stack; we'll still take the SDK snippets for the integration test harness.
[04:30] Priya (Argon): on data retention, by default hosted logs are kept 30 days; we need to ensure logs containing PII are not stored or are encrypted.
[04:43] Maya (Redwood): configurable retention and field redaction options exist; for the pilot we can set retention to zero for request logs and enable customer-managed keys. we'll capture exact requirements in the security questionnaire.
[04:58] Ethan (Redwood): moving to benchmarks — propose the following plan: week 0 (this week) align scope and dataset; week 1 integrate endpoint + run smoke tests; week 2 run full benchmarks (throughput/latency/accuracy) on hosted and optionally dedicated; week 3 iterate on prompts and quantization; week 4 run final validation and produce report.
[05:20] Liam (Argon): timeline sounds reasonable. question on dedicated vs hosted — we need to understand unit economics differences.
[05:30] Maya (Redwood): we'll include pricing scenarios. hosted is fastest to spin up; dedicated (reserved capacity) gives better predictable throughput and possibly lower per-token cost for sustained workloads. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles to reduce cost while preserving accuracy.
[05:50] Sofia (Argon): for tool calling — we need the output to be strict JSON schema (no extra text) because we pipe it into our downstream parsers. can your function calling guarantee structured output?
[06:05] Ethan (Redwood): yes, we have a structured-output mode and function-calling options to enforce JSON-only responses, plus schema validation on the server side. small caveat: model hallucinations can still produce malformed JSON, so we recommend a two-step pattern: 1) function call to get structured fields, 2) run a lightweight validator that checks schema and re-asks if necessary. we also provide heuristics to coerce common minor errors.
[06:35] Sofia (Argon): ok that works. do you support streaming structured output? we need low latency when users are live.
[06:44] Ethan (Redwood): streaming is supported; with our SDK you get chunked JSON streaming and can reconstruct objects client-side as they arrive. with OpenAI-compatible endpoint you can stream too but the SDK smooths out partial tokens and provides event hooks.
[07:02] Maya (Redwood): on metrics — we'll capture P95 and P99 latency, tokens/sec, accuracy per field, and cost per 1k requests. those will be our success metrics.
[07:18] Liam (Argon): for workload sizing — estimated 50 rps sustained, peak 150 for short bursts. how many GPUs would that be?
[07:27] Ethan (Redwood): depends on model choice and quantization. e.g. a quantized 7B model on an A100-like instance with batched inference can handle X rps — we'll size during week 2 benchmarks. if you want guaranteed capacity we can reserve a pool; for pilot hosted is likely fine.
[07:50] Sofia (Argon): concerned about latency spikes that we saw in other vendors, esp during cold starts. do you do warm pools or cache priming?
[07:59] Ethan (Redwood): yes — we support warm workers, KV cache priming for common prefixes, and pre-warming on rollout. part of the benchmark is to measure cold-start and steady-state latencies.
[08:14] Priya (Argon): SOC2 report and pen test evidence?
[08:20] Maya (Redwood): we'll attach our SOC2 Type II report and recent penetration test summary as part of the security pack, plus the KMS integration doc.
[08:35] Sofia (Argon): great. one more on the function/tool calling: we might want the model to call internal tools for enrichment (e.g., lookup merchant ID). is that supported?
[08:47] Ethan (Redwood): yes — tool-calling patterns supported. you can register tools with descriptions and schemas; the model can return tool invocation JSON which you execute server-side and feed back results. there are also permissions and RBAC controls to limit which tools a model can call.
[09:05] Liam (Argon): what's the dev velocity like — how long to get a simple end-to-end test running?
[09:12] Maya (Redwood): if you use the OpenAI-compatible endpoint and your existing shim, you might have a smoke test in a day. with SDK and deeper integrations (streaming, function calling) plan 2-3 days to wire and run initial smoke tests.
[09:28] Sofia (Argon): ok good. on schema we expect: merchant_name, total_amount, date, tax, currency, items[]. items array should include name, qty, price. we need field-level accuracy metrics.
[09:43] Ethan (Redwood): noted — please include that in the sample spec you'll share. we'll set up eval harness to compute precision/recall per field.
[09:55] Maya (Redwood): i'll follow up with a POC scope doc that outlines the eval harness, dataset format, and success criteria.
[10:05] Sofia (Argon): thanks. regarding telemetry — we need per-route latency traces and token-level cost breakdown for the pilot.
[10:17] Ethan (Redwood): Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per model/route, and tracing hooks — we'll share dashboard access for the pilot.
[10:30] Priya (Argon): auth — we'll need SSO and RBAC, plus audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, is that possible?
[10:40] Maya (Redwood): yes — we support SAML SSO, RBAC roles, and audit log exports to external SIEMs. we'll include configuration docs.
[10:55] Liam (Argon): any gotchas with OpenAI compatibility we should watch for?
[11:00] Ethan (Redwood): mostly around some optional fields and advanced streaming semantics. also batching semantics differ; if you rely on OpenAI's batch nuances you'll want to test. our SDK will handle optimal batching by default.
[11:15] Sofia (Argon): can you do a brief demo of the function calling mapping? maybe in the follow-up demo?
[11:21] Maya (Redwood): yes we can schedule a 30-min demo with a quick walkthrough of SDK vs endpoint function calls. i'll include that as part of next steps.
[11:32] Ethan (Redwood): one technical note on structured outputs: we recommend schema-first function definitions and a small validation layer — usually solves 95% of malformed outputs. for the remaining edge cases we often use a deterministic post-processing step.
[11:50] Sofia (Argon): got it. pricing note — for the pilot we need a capped spend and usage alerts.
[11:58] Maya (Redwood): we'll propose a pilot pricing with budget cap and usage alerts.
[12:08] Priya (Argon): in terms of deployment options for later production, we may need Private deployment inside our VPC. can we run a private control plane?
[12:18] Maya (Redwood): yes, Redwood Private offers a private control plane and VPC/on-prem packages. we'll include high-level deployment options and costs.
[12:32] Liam (Argon): for benchmarking, what metrics do you need from our side?
[12:38] Ethan (Redwood): sample dataset (OCR outputs), expected schema, throughput targets, and any special corner-case examples. also whether you want to test on hosted first or go straight to dedicated.
[12:52] Sofia (Argon): we'll do hosted first, then dedicated if results need it.
[12:58] Maya (Redwood): ok wrap up — recap and next steps: we'll send POC scope, SDK samples, security docs, and schedule benchmark run and a short demo.
[13:12] Sofia (Argon): sounds good. thanks all.
[13:18] Maya (Redwood): thanks everyone. end.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker labels simplified; some words may be transcribed phonetically (eg Redwood Dedictaed).

End of transcript.

POC Timeline (as discussed):
Week 0: align scope & dataset (send docs)
Week 1: integration + smoke tests (OpenAI-compatible endpoint + SDK snippets)
Week 2: full benchmarks (latency/throughput/accuracy) hosted and optional dedicated
Week 3: iterate on prompts/quantization & run targeted experiments
Week 4: final validation, report, and decision on production deployment

Success Criteria (agreed):
- Field-level extraction accuracy >= 95% on key fields
- End-to-end P95 latency < 250ms for receipts
- Sustained throughput target: 50 rps, handle bursts to 150 rps
- Schema conformity for structured outputs >= 98% after validator

References / Links Mentioned:
- Security pack (to be attached)
- SDK snippets & OpenAI-compatible endpoint examples (Ethan to share)
- Sample POC scope doc (Maya to send)
- Redwood Console demo link (to be shared)
